---
title: "Part 3 - HLAtools"
---

# HLAtools is an R package for working with the IPD-IMGT/HLA Database: allele names, versions, and, most usefully, the sequence alignments. Today we'll use it to look at the amino acid sequences of HLA-DPB1, which sets us up for the app at the end.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(HLAtools)
```

# First, we download the DPB1 protein alignment straight from the IPD-IMGT/HLA Database (this needs an internet connection and takes a few seconds). We ask for a specific database version, so the results are the same every time we run it.
# The other HLAtools search functions look for the alignments in an object named "HLAalignments", so that's what we call it.

```{r}
HLAalignments <- alignmentFull(loci = "DPB1", alignType = "prot", version = "3.65.0")
```

# What amino acids does DPB1*04:01:01:01 have at positions 84 through 87? This is one of the three major DPB1 antibody epitopes. The answer is written position-then-amino-acid, joined by "~": "84G" means glycine (G) at position 84.

```{r}
alignmentSearch("prot", "DPB1*04:01:01:01", 84:87)
```

# Compare a few alleles side by side at the positions that make up the 55 and 84 epitopes.

```{r}
customAlign(
  "prot",
  c("DPB1*02:01:02:01", "DPB1*03:01:01:01", "DPB1*04:01:01:01", "DPB1*04:02:01:01"),
  c(55:57, 84:87)
)
```

# If time allows: where do two alleles differ? compareSequences() lists every position where they are not the same.

```{r}
compareSequences("prot", c("DPB1*04:01:01:01", "DPB1*04:02:01:01"))
```

# If time allows: how many of the DPB1 alleles in the database have each amino acid at position 84? This counts allele names, not how often each is seen in people. "." means there is no residue there, mostly null alleles whose protein stops early.

```{r}
queryPositions("prot", "DPB1", 84, table = TRUE)
```

# And going the other way: which alleles carry the GGPM motif at 84 to 87? Notice that null (N) and questionable (Q) alleles show up too: the motif is in the DNA sequence even if the protein isn't expressed.

```{r}
motifMatch("DPB1*84G~85G~86P~87M", "prot", full = FALSE) |>  # full = FALSE gives two-field names
  head(20)
```

# This is the kind of question that used to mean downloading a text file and counting columns by hand. Now it is one line of code, it is repeatable, and it updates when the database does: just change the version number.

# Next, we will turn this into a small app that anyone in the lab can use, without writing any code. See the "app" folder.
